items.title: verify-merge heavy-gate classifier and compile-once optimization
items.context: scripts/verify-merge-needed.sh classifies a diff via ci-classify-changes.sh and reports whether it would trigger CI's heavy Linux build/test gate without running the full merge gate; scripts/verify-merge.sh runs the same classifier for context, installs once, builds the web host only when stale, compiles test artifacts once and reuses the compiled output for test:unit/test:packages, and gates native package tests behind the same portability classification CI uses, while preserving every pre-existing required step (validate-pack, workspace/extension coverage, the pi-ai vitest suite, integration, e2e). Also documents the new advisory script in CONTRIBUTING.md and two docs/dev guides, and adds scripts/__tests__/verify-merge.test.mjs. 2026-08-24: rebased onto upstream/main (base e28218e4, up from the original 91-commits-behind base 4bbfb31f) after fast-forwarding fork main; hit a REAL merge conflict with an unrelated upstream fix (#1582/#1883, building the native test-fault-injection addon on a fresh checkout, gated behind a rustc check) that landed on the same lines this branch touches. Resolved by combining both: classify step runs first, then the native-addon build/Rust-check, then install, preserving the addon-staging step (mkdir/cp/export GSD_NATIVE_PREFER_LOCAL) before test:unit:compiled. Verified via git range-diff and rev-list --left-right --count (0 1). Cross-AI reviewed with `codex review --commit` (codex-cli 0.145.0, using its own tool access to inspect build-web-if-stale.cjs and ci-classify-changes.sh) and an independent Claude Opus 4.6 subagent pass; both found real, non-overlapping issues, which were fixed and folded into the commit via amend: (1) verify-merge-needed.sh now guards --base/--head against a missing value instead of an unbound-variable crash, (2) verify-merge-needed.sh now warns (not fails) when the working tree has uncommitted/untracked changes, since its classification is diff-based and can't see them, (3) added 4 new behavioral tests for both fixes (10/10 pass locally). Two additional codex findings were verified accurate but deliberately NOT fixed here (out of scope, pre-existing bugs in files this branch doesn't own): build-web-if-stale.cjs's mtime-based staleness check doesn't cover packages/*, the lockfile, or scripts/stage-web-standalone.cjs, so it can under-rebuild; ci-classify-changes.sh silently falls back to `HEAD~1` if BASE/HEAD don't resolve, which can under-classify a multi-commit diff on a shallow/misconfigured checkout. Both are noted in a comment in verify-merge-needed.sh and should get their own dedicated fix later.
items.validation: Local: bash -n syntax-checked all scripts; node --test scripts/__tests__/verify-merge.test.mjs passed 12/12 (10 from the review round plus 2 more for the exit-128 fail-safe fix). items.title: Repair evidence-backed lifecycle shadow authority before Milestone validation
items.context: Adopted Milestones could contain legacy-complete Tasks or Slices with durable completion evidence but no workflow_item_lifecycles authority, causing strict closeout validation to fail with missing canonical lifecycle authority. items.title: subagent resume fails with unhelpful error for fresh-context runs (no sessionFile ever recorded)
items.context: Parent subagent resume attempt for succeeded run 60a4e9a8-8a64-4a99-84e8-a7b661a831ea failed with 'Resume requires exactly one child session or an agent selector. Available resumable agents: none'. Investigated as a possible upstream selector-prefix bug (prior debug session referenced a nonexistent 'W075' claiming a canonical-selector fix was already applied). No such item or fix exists anywhere in the governance register, worktrees, or fork branches (checked all 61 register items, 10 active worktrees, origin/upstream/w014/w018 remotes). The headless.ts prefix-matching code (resolveResumeSession, startsWith-based) is unrelated: it resolves CLI `--resume <prefix>` arguments for session files on disk, not the subagent tool's in-process 'resume' action, and was never the code path involved.
items.validation: 2026-10-08: traced the actual mechanism in src/resources/extensions/subagent/index.ts (action:'resume', ~line 1114) and launch.ts (resolveSubagentSessionArgs/createSubagentLaunchPlan). A child's sessionFile is only ever populated when the dispatch's effective contextMode is 'fork' (index.ts:655/869 only set currentResult.sessionFile when launch.session.mode === 'fork'). The failing run's persisted record has contextMode:'fresh' (the tool default) and mode:'single', so the one child never had a sessionFile, and action:'resume' filters record.children by `child.sessionFile` truthiness (index.ts:1138) -- with zero matches it always reports 'Available resumable agents: none', regardless of how many children exist or whether an agent selector is passed. This matches documented behavior (docs/user-docs/subagents.md:66-68: fork 'branches from the current parent session'; resume depends on a persisted child session file) but the resulting tool error message gives no hint that the run needs to have been launched with context:'fork' to ever be resumable -- a caller who launched with the default 'fresh' context (the common case) cannot resume no matter what selector they pass. This is a documented-constraint / UX-clarity gap, not a selector-resolution defect. No code bug found; no fix applied.

localExtensionPatches.knownIssue: On gsd-pi <=1.16.0, this directory-based global extension was silently destroyed on EVERY gsd session start: pruneRemovedBundledExtensions() in src/resource-loader.ts runs a 'sweep' step that rmSync()s (recursive, force) any subdirectory under ~/.gsd/agent/extensions/ whose name isn't part of gsd's own currently-bundled extension set, with no exclusion for community-tier manifests. Reproduced 2026-08-24 with a trivial, harmless test extension (no filesystem code of its own) -- gsd itself deleted the whole directory after one `gsd --print` session, silently (all wrapped in try/catch, no stderr). `gsd --version` alone did not trigger it (exits before initResources()); any full session-starting invocation did. Temporarily worked around via project-local .gsd/extensions/<name>.js (ecosystem/loader.ts has no prune/sweep logic), installed only in local workspace. CONFIRMED FIXED in 1.16.1 (upgraded global install from 1.16.0 -> 1.16.1 on 2026-08-24 via `npm install -g @opengsd/gsd-pi@latest`; re-tested the exact same reproduction with a fresh dummy extension and it survived a full gsd --print session). Reverted to the documented global location as the sole install afterward and removed the project-local workaround. requires.platform is now set to >=1.16.1 so this manifest self-documents the minimum safe version. Still plausibly worth an upstream bug report so gsd-pi's own manifest-spec.md / building-extensions.md Quick Start docs (or the sweep logic itself, for anyone still on <=1.16.0) reflect this -- NOT filed, needs explicit authorization first per contributor governance.
